_comment: Keys must exactly match the 'Plant___Disease' folder names your trained model uses (see models/class_indices.json after training). These starter entries are examples for a few classes per crop — expand this file to cover every class you actually train on. Content here is general agronomic guidance, not a substitute for local agricultural extension advice.

Mango___Anthracnose.symptoms: Dark, sunken, irregular spots on leaves, twigs, and fruit; spots may merge and cause leaf blight in humid weather.
Mango___Anthracnose.causes: Fungus Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, favored by high humidity and rain during flowering/fruiting.
Mango___Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves/twigs; spray neem oil (2%) or Bordeaux mixture at 7-10 day intervals during wet periods.
Mango___Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Carbendazim or Mancozeb-based fungicide sprays as per label dosage, especially before flowering.
Mango___Anthracnose.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid excess nitrogen, which promotes soft, disease-prone growth.
Mango___Anthracnose.watering: Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day; water at the base to keep foliage dry.
Mango___Anthracnose.prevention: Prune for good airflow, remove fallen debris, apply preventive copper sprays before the rainy season.
Mango___Anthracnose.future_care: Monitor new flushes closely during monsoon; repeat preventive sprays each season.

Mango___Healthy.symptoms: No visible lesions, discoloration, or deformation; leaf color and texture are uniform.
Mango___Healthy.fertilizer: Continue standard seasonal NPK schedule for mango.
Mango___Healthy.watering: Maintain regular irrigation matched to the current growth stage.
Mango___Healthy.prevention: Continue routine monitoring and orchard sanitation.
Mango___Healthy.future_care: Re-check periodically, especially after weather changes.

Coconut___Bud_Rot.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of the spear leaf, foul smell from the crown, eventual collapse of the bud region.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.causes: Phytophthora palmivora fungus, spreads rapidly in prolonged wet/humid conditions.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.organic_treatment: Remove and burn severely affected tissue; drench crown with Bordeaux mixture or neem-based biofungicide.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride or Metalaxyl-MZ drenching in the crown region as per local agricultural extension guidance.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.fertilizer: Balanced palm-specific NPK plus micronutrients (boron, magnesium) to support recovery.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.watering: Improve drainage around the base; avoid waterlogging.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.prevention: Ensure good drainage, avoid injuring the crown, apply preventive copper spray before monsoon.
Coconut___Bud_Rot.future_care: Inspect crown region monthly during rainy season; isolate severely affected palms.

Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Small gray-to-brown spots with yellow halos on leaflets, coalescing into larger blighted patches.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.causes: Pestalotiopsis palmarum fungus, worsened by nutrient deficiency and water stress.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.organic_treatment: Remove heavily infected leaflets; apply neem oil spray at first sign of spotting.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil-based fungicide as per label instructions.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.fertilizer: Correct potassium and magnesium deficiencies, which increase susceptibility.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.watering: Maintain consistent irrigation; avoid drought stress.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Balanced fertilization and removal of dead fronds to reduce fungal spore sources.
Coconut___Gray_Leaf_Spot.future_care: Recheck new fronds each month during dry-to-wet season transitions.

Areca_Nut___Healthy.symptoms: Uniform green leaf color, no lesions, spots, or wilting.
Areca_Nut___Healthy.fertilizer: Continue standard seasonal NPK schedule for areca palms.
Areca_Nut___Healthy.watering: Maintain regular irrigation for the current season.
Areca_Nut___Healthy.prevention: Continue routine monitoring and plantation sanitation.
Areca_Nut___Healthy.future_care: Re-check periodically, especially after heavy rain.

Areca_Nut___Koleroga.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on nuts and leaves that turn brown-black; affected nuts drop prematurely (also known as fruit rot / mahali disease).
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.causes: Phytophthora meadii/palmivora fungus, spreads fast in wet, humid, poorly ventilated plantations.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.organic_treatment: Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture on bunches before monsoon onset; remove and destroy fallen infected nuts.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride spray on bunches as per local agricultural extension recommendations.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.fertilizer: Balanced NPK with adequate potassium to strengthen plant resistance.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.watering: Improve plantation drainage; avoid water stagnation around the base.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.prevention: Thin out dense plantings for airflow, apply preventive Bordeaux spray before each monsoon.
Areca_Nut___Koleroga.future_care: Repeat preventive spraying every monsoon season; monitor bunches weekly during wet months.
